summary: Peter van der Veer is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Groningen and Utrecht University, later serving as professor at Utrecht, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, University of Amsterdam, and director at the Max Planck Institute (2008–2021).

Peter von Bohlen was an Indologist who studied under August Wilhelm Schlegel, Georg Wilhelm Freytag, and Franz Bopp, attending Halle, Bonn, Berlin, and Königsberg. He served as professor of oriental literature at the University of Königsberg from 1825 until his death.

Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Leo Meyer and Rudolf von Roth at Dorpat, Tübingen, Jena, Leipzig, and Giessen. He served as an associate professor at the University of Giessen from 1886 to 1896.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied as a pupil under Heinz Bechert and served as a research fellow at the Academy of Sciences and Literature, Mainz, around 1993.

Petra Maurer is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. Her career includes posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013) and the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Phakchok Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who earned a Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute and studied under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje. He serves as Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.

Phanit Jetjiravat is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under academic advisors Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.

Philip A. Kuhn was a sinologist and historian who studied at Harvard, SOAS, and Georgetown. He served on the faculty of the University of Chicago (1963–1978) and Harvard University from 1978, directing the Fairbank Center for Chinese Studies (1980–1986).

Philip A. Mellor is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Manchester by 1989 and was attested in 2010 as Professor and Head of the School of Humanities at the University of Leeds.

Philip Boas Yampolsky was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and earned his degrees at Columbia University, where he served as a Japanese lecturer and East Asian Library librarian (1968–1994/1996).

Philip Clart is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied under Daniel L. Overmyer from 1990 to 1996 and was appointed Professor of Chinese Culture and History at Leipzig University around 2008.
Philip Deslippe is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed his PhD and served as a teaching associate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2020).

Philip Kapleau was a religious and Buddhist studies teacher. He studied under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki, Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani, Soen Nakagawa, and Sogaku Daiun Harada, and founded the Rochester Zen Center and Chapin Mill Retreat Center.

Philip L. Quinn was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Georgetown, Delaware, and Pittsburgh. He served on the faculty at Brown University (1970–1985) and held the O'Brien Professorship at the University of Notre Dame from 1985.

Philip Lutgendorf is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (1976–1987). He joined the University of Iowa faculty in 1985 and served as president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (2010–2018).

Philip Whalen was an author and Buddhist studies figure who graduated from Reed College and studied under Richard Baker. He held posts as resident teacher at South Ridge Zendo (1974–1975) and abbot of Hartford Street Zen Center (1991).

Philipp André Maas is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under Claus Vogel and Albrecht Wezler. He has held academic posts at Bonn, the University of Vienna, and Leipzig University (attested 2022).

Philippe Stern was an art historian and Indologist. Throughout his career, he held prominent posts at the Musée Guimet (1927–1965), the Musée de la parole et du geste (1928–1938), and the École du Louvre (1929–1965).

Philippe Turenne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at McGill University under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and studied under teachers including Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche, Richard P. Hayes, and Kameshwar Nath Mishra.

Philippe-Édouard Foucaux was a Tibetologist and Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He served as Professor of Tibetan at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (from 1842) and Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1857–1894).
